properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/10/2023 to CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC in Tuscarora Twp, Bradford county. 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: CHESAPEAKE APPALACHIA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 1/24/2023
Violation Code: 78.56(a) - PITS AND TANKS FOR TEMPORARY CONTAINMENT - Operator failed to contain pollutional substances and wastes from the drilling, altering, completing, recompleting, servicing and plugging the well, including brines, drill cuttings, drilling muds, oils, stimulation fluids, well treatment and servicing fluids, plugging and drilling fluids other than gases in a pit, tank or series of pits and tanks.
Violation ID: 987670
Permit API: 015-23717
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Tuscarora Twp
Inspection Type: Administrative/File Review
Inspection Date: 3/10/2023
Comments: On 3/10/2023, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an Administrative inspection on the Chesapeake Floydie well site. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected from water puddles on the south corner and northeast side of the Floydie well site. During an inspection on 1/24/2023, the department discovered high conductance fluid on two areas of the well pad surface outside of containment. In the first area, the fluid covered a 6' x 10' area and field tested at 11.93 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. The department collected water sample #9551-039 for laboratory analysis from location N 41.665131 W -76.126503. In the second area, the fluid covered a 10' x 10' area and field tested at 4.90 mS conductance with an Oakton PCTS-50 meter. This water puddle was in a larger muddy 35' x 20' area that field tested at over 4.0 mS conductance with a Hanna Groline meter. The department collected water sample #9551-040 from location N 41.66589 W -76.12645.On 2/25/2023 the department received the results of the laboratory analysis that shows elevated barium, strontium and lithium and is indicative of brine/production fluid being released onto the pad. The sample reports are displayed in pictures 1, 2, 3 and 4.Chesapeake is pursuing Act 2 for the site in response to that incident.The release of fluid with elevated conductance to the pad surface constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78.66(b)(2).Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3492400 for elevated conductance fluid being discovered on the unprotected pad surface.

properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 10/04/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Township, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 10/04/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8161542
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/04/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted after the operator reported a release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from GPU #3 on 9/18/23. An area between GPU #3 and the southwest pad edge has been excavated including in the stormwater channel at the pad edge. Some fluid was present in the channel which had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 910 uS/cm. On Pad A, an area of secondary containment has been set up for the excavated pad material. The material has been tarped. The containment appears to be in good condition.Six wells are staged for production on Pad A. Six GPUs are present and appear to be in good condition.On Pad B, nine wells are staged for production. Nine GPUs are present within secondary containment. The GPUs and containment appear to be in good condition. Multiple batteries of frac tanks are present on the pad within secondary containment. A few puddles of fluid are present on the pad surface in front of the frac tank batteries which had an EC between 2.40 to 2.50 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up the fluid. The EC of the fluid in the sump at the east end of the north stormwater channel has an EC of 1645 uS/cm.Along the access road, vegetation has germinated where excavation took place after a truck rollover caused a release of produced fluid to an area surrounding the access road. The area is not yet permanently stabilized. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21855 for release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad A from 9/18/23.Violations remain outstanding for the release to Pad B from 2/3/23.

Comments: On October 2, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of K Petroleum Inc's Patterson 1 well site located in Nottingham Township, Washington County.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a well tag with all required information posted on it fixed to the wellhead on site. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the wellhead. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a meter box and separator on site. The meter box was observed to have a well posting fixed to it with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this meter box and separator.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a production tank within an earthen dike. An approximately 6 ft by 4 ft area on the ground at the base of the production tank where the valve is located was observed to be lacking vegetative cover. Pieces of the valve appeared to be broken off and was observed to be laying on the ground adjacent to the production tank. At the time of this inspection, an orange sheeny substance was observed to be actively dripping from the valve onto the ground around the production tank. The ground in this area was observed to be stained a dark black color with pooling of the orange substance observed directly below the valve. At the time of this inspection the Department utilized a conductivity meter to screen the ground in this release area. Soil conductivity readings of 0.460 mS, 0.237 mS, 0.329 mS, and 0.308 mS were collected and compared to a background soil conductivity readings of 0.0635 mS collected in a vegetated area adjacent to the well site. These soil conductivity readings are elevated when compared to the background soil conductivity reading, which further subjugates that a release has occurred in this area. While on site, the Department called the number listed on the well tag/well posting as well as K Petroleum Inc's Robert Inghram. The Department was not able to reach either via phone, therefore the Department left a voicemail for each regarding the findings during today's inspection.The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the Operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Based one today's inspection, violations are being issued for a release from the production tank.

One production tank was present onsite, however appeared to be unconnected and not in use. There also appeared to be a a another GPU behind the 5H GPU and the Department was unable to discern if it was in use. A barrel of methanol was also observed onsite and did not appear to be with in secondary containment. The Department recommends ensuring all regulated substances are placed with in proper secondary containment, and remove any equipment not necessary for production from the site. Ms.Empfield stated she would get an Act 9 sign ordered and installed at the site as well as ensure field staff assess the site and correct any issues as needed.Based on todays inspection, violations are being issued for the Act 9 sign, observed corrosion on the GPU, production equipment on site not in use, and the regulated substance(s) not in secondary containment.

Violation ID: 8259770
Permit API: 051-24048
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Compliance Schedule Evaluation
Inspection Date: 12/18/2025
Comments: On December 18, 2025, the Department conducted a Compliance Schedule Evaluation of Diversified's Yasenosky 2 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County. This plugged well site is under the March 7, 2019 COA (enf ID 372946).According to Department records, this well was plugged on 2/17/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 11/17/2025 and a well site restoration report should be submitted to the Department by 1/16/2026.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox at the access road entrance that had an erosion and sediment control plan for plugging operations at the Yasenosky 2 plugged well site within it. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the access road for plugged well site to be graveled and not restored. This gravel road led to the plugged well site's approximate coordinate location which appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth and was not exhibiting any erosion or sedimentation issues. At the time of this inspection, the well site appeared to be exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. The Department observed a pipeline riser and a pipeline marker to be present in the middle of the plugged well site and compost filter sock was observed downslope and at the edge of the plugged well site's perimeter.At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that the well site is fully restored. The Department recommends the Operator restore the access road to its 70% uniform and adequate vegetative requirement or submit a completed and signed Landowner Waiver of Well Site Restoration form to the Department, the Department also recommends the Operator remove all erosion and sediment control features from the well site and submit a Well Site Restoration Report by the 1/16/2025 deadline.Based on today's inspection, and the well site not being fully restored, violations are being issued for failure to comply with a COA of the Department.

Violation ID: 8180970
Permit API: 015-23842
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Herrick Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/26/2024
Comments: Southwestern's (SWN's) reported to the DEP reporting hotline at ~ 1705 hours on 03/22/2024 that a vendor ripped containment liner while moving hoses during demobilization activities. Ponded rain water ran from containment onto newly exposed soil/gravel. It is believed rainwater came into contact with brine contaminated site equipment releasing approx. 20 to 30 gallons.On 03/26/2024 the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an incident inspection of SWN's VanOrder-Patrick (12 Pad) Well Pad located in Herrick Township, Bradford County. The weather was 47 degrees and partly cloudy. I arrived at 1010 hours. This inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to DEP by SWN.On 03/26/2024 I spoke with Mike Deming a SWN representative who said the release was ~1-2 barrels. Photos #2-6 show the progression of the remediation process from 03/22/2024 to 03/26/2024. SWN reported that the highest conductivity reading after the release was ~21 mS/cm. The red dumpster seen in photo #6 is lined and holds the recovered material. Due to active operations during the time of this inspection access to the spill area was not possible. SWN representatives were present during the time of the inspection. SWN representatives said they are currently working on drill outs. They have completed the plugs for one of the three new wells. They plan to finish within two weeks. Pooled water on the pad was field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 428-839 us/cm. Pooled water within the off loading secondary containment was field measured for EC at ~ 2.7 mS/cm. The DEP reported the findings to SWN representatives who said that it would be taken care of right away. Based on the reported release quantity this is being referred to Act 2 for compliance. Based on the reported release violations of the following are cited against API #015-23842 at this time:35 P.S. 691.402(b)35 P.S. 6018.30125 Pa. Code 78a.56(a)I departed at 1050 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/06/2023 to EQT ARO LLC in McIntyre Twp, Lycoming county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/06/2023
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 984603
Permit API: 081-21879
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: McIntyre Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/06/2023
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification received on February 3, 2023 from the operator of a release of produced fluid to the pad surface and access road of Pad B from clam boxes which were being removed from the location. Two snubbing units are in operation on Pad B. I met with company man Josh Scheihing upon arriving on Pad B. He showed me where on the access road the release had occurred. The surface had already been scraped at the time of this inspection. No fluid was observed in this area. Some clam shell boxes were present along the access road near the area that had been scraped. According to the operator, these boxes were empty and were slated to be removed. I walked the rest of the site with the company man. The fluid in the sump at the northeast stormwater channel outlet was frozen. There was snow and ice present in the northeast corner of the pad but no fluid was observed. The majority of the pad surface was dry or had snow and ice on it. I found an area along the east side of the pad with fluid with an electrical conductivity (EC) of greater than 19.99 mS/cm near a trailer for MidAtlantic Energy Services. The farther away from the trailer I took EC readings, the more the EC decreased. At the farthest north point of the fluid puddle, the EC was 1977 uS/cm and at the farther point to the south the EC was 2.74 mS/cm. I took sample 0718-203 from the area next to the MidAtlantic Energy Services trailer to be analyzed for SAC 942 plus Br, Li, and Al. I let the company man know what I found before leaving the location. I called Rick Hall of EQT on the same day after leaving the location to let him know what I found. On the same day, Zac Subra of EQT sent me an email which stated that they had done their own investigation on the pad and had found out that MidAtlantic Energy Services used ice melt to melt the ice around their trailer. EQT believes that this caused the elevated electrical conductivity. The email included photos of the ice melt used. Also on the same day the operator notified the Department that fluid with a high electrical conductivity was found beneath rig mats on the pad. The notification stated that the operator believed that this fluid may be associated with the release from the clam shell boxes which occurred on 2/3/23 since the clam shells had been stored on the dancefloor prior to being moved off of the pad. The operator estimated the volume of this fluid at 42 gallons. Due to the estimated volume of the release, the Department recommends pursuing Act 2 remediation for this release.Violations noted for the release from the clam shell boxes to Pad B and the Pad B access road.

Comments: On Thursday, 9/18/2025, I conducted an inspection of the Oil and Gas Management, Inc. Brown 2 well, permit number 005-29119, due to complaint received 9/16/2025 (CTS #392326). The site is located in the woods off of Chestnut Road in Parks township, Armstrong county. The complaint was submitted as a result of a spill on the site. The spill appears to be used motor oil and I estimated that more than 25 gallons was spilled. This was due to containers (2 - 5 gallon buckets and a 55 gallon drum) and refuse (used oil filter) observed in the immediate area of the spill (see pictures 3, 4, and 5). The operator did not report the spill and it appears that the operator has not visited the site recently. The well was shut in on the day of the inspection, but the operator did report a non-averaged production of 729.0 mcf for the 2024 production (365 days producing, as per OGRE). The well appeared to be disconnected from the compressor (see picture 9) and the compressor does not appear to be functional at this time (no motor, see picture 8). It needs to be noted that the production chart is dated 4-2-23 (see picture 3). The site access road is also in terrible condition. The E and S BMP's have not been maintained and there are multiple areas that are deeply rutted and have significant accelerated erosion.As a result of the site conditions, the operator is being cited for violations to 25 PA Code 78.53, 102.22(a), 102.4(b)(1), 78.57(a), 78.66(b), and CSL 402(b)

Report Details

Violation Code: 102.4(b)4 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person failed to plan and implement earth disturbance activities to minimize duration & extent of earth disturbance, minimize soil compaction, maximize protection of drainage features and vegetation, and utilize other measures or controls that prevent or minimize the generation of increased stormwater runoff.
Violation ID: 8266973
Permit API: 125-28214
Unconventional: Yes
County: Washington
Municipality: Amwell Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/04/2026
Comments: On 03/04/2026, a routine partial inspection was conducted at the Cashdollar Well Site.The following was observed:I observed accelerated erosion on the access road. Near the upper portion of the access road, sediment laden water was traveling towards the adjacent vegetation. It appeared to end within the brush. I observed accumulated road fines and gravel within the vegetation (Photos 1-6). Third party disturbance had been noted on site.Accelerated erosion and sedimentation was also observed near the beginning of the access road (Photos 7-14).The accelerated erosion was leading towards a stream and culvert. Gravel was observed in the vegetation above the culvert outlet. It did not appear that sediment was entering the stream at the time of inspection, however it is likely to with additional precipitation (Photos 15-18).The stream water upstream of the culvert appeared mildly turbid (Photos 19-21).Pooling on the access road was observed below the accelerated erosion (Photos 22).The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan was on site (Photo 23).Violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a), 102.4(b)4, and 78a.53 are being issued for the accelerated erosion and sedimentation observed on the access road.

Violation ID: 8162196
Permit API: 065-25518
Unconventional: No
County: Jefferson
Municipality: Knox Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 10/17/2023
Comments: This site located west off Odonnell Road, 1 1/2 miles south of railroad crossing on State Game Lands Road, at the end of second branch to the north. Well is set-up for production with a meter, separator and one tank. A report of a release of 32 gallons of produced water was reported by Will Warfel with Diversified Prod LLC at 12:30 on 9/21/23 at this well site. The release was assumed to be from the separator, there is an area of no vegetation around the well head, separator and meter and a path 70x15' path to the west. Contaminated soil needs to be removed from site and hauled to a licensed disposal facility. This follow-up inspection by WQS Taylor showed no additional clean-up activity has been completed at this site. The previous inspection detailed increased conductivity levels in areas around the well head, separator and in an area of dead vegetation west of the well set-up. Conductivity tested in vegetated area west of well head read 106 micro siemansClean-up of this site is not completed and will require Act 2 SOP to remediate this site.

Violation ID: 870427
Permit API: 015-23420

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2019-12-09
Comments: The DEP conducted a follow-up inspection of Repsol's Monro G 03-142 well site located in Columbia Twp, Bradford County on 12/9/2019 at 0940 hours. The weather was 39 degrees with cloudy skies. The inspection was conducted to follow up on site conditions in relation to the violations cited on 4/25/2019. John Ciccone, WQS Trainee, was onsite with me for the inspection. We inspected the entire site for flowback activities. Some wells still have separators attached to them. PCSM BMPs are present onsite and appear to be functioning as designed. No issues with containments were found today. The majority of the site was snow and ice covered. On 4/25/2019, the DEP cited violations for a release of frac fluid and sand after an iron washout created a powerful jet stream of fluids which tore through containments. The total volume of the release was estimated to be 15 gallons. A drop-pipe was installed into the area of the release to continue to collect impacted water from the ground. Onsite today, the DEP observed this drop-pipe (see photo#4). No fluids could be field measured today. Due to the drop-pipe remaining, it is believed that follow-up sampling has not been conducted by the operator yet. Due to the clean-up of the release not being confirmed and the drop-pipe remaining, the violations noted on 4/25/2019 will remain open and are cited as outstanding. We departed the site at 1030 hours.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/16/2026 to INR OPR LLC in Young Township, Indiana county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: INR OPR LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/16/2026
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8271105
Permit API: 063-37560
Unconventional: Yes
County: Indiana
Municipality: Young Township
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/16/2026
Comments: Spencer Johnson (Infinity Natural Resources) reported a 1-5 barrel (42-210 gallons) production fluid release at the Jost Van Dyke (JVD) well pad on 4/14/2026 while conducting a water transfer. I met Spencer at the JVD well pad on 4/16/2026. He showed me the impacted area. Excavation began to remediate the spill area, and soil field readings were collected. He stated the spill occurred when contractors were tearing down the storage tank. Production water was spilled out of containment. It did not leave the pad. He indicated INR intends to attain an Act 2 standard for this cleanup. Due to the spill being greater than 42 gallons, the Department is requesting remediation and attainment of an Act 2 standard. Tipping receipts and waste manifests are requested by the Department associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from this spill.Violations are noted below.
